strengths: Addresses the first practical watermarking solution for diffusion language models, a novel and timely problem given the rapid adoption of DLMs
Strong theoretical foundation with elegant constrained optimization formulation (Eq. 1) and rigorous solution (Theorem 3.1) that recovers Red-Green ARLM watermarks in restricted case
Intuitive decomposition into expectation boost and predictive bias terms provides clear understanding of how the watermark operates

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple models (LLADA-8B, DREAM-7B, DREAMON), extensive ablations, robustness testing against text modifications, and superior performance vs. order-agnostic baselines
Practical algorithm with minimal generation overhead (~15s vs ~9s baseline) and efficient hash computation via FFT
Excellent reproducibility: code promised, extensive experimental details in appendices, clear hyperparameter specifications
Achieves >99% TPR@1% FPR with careful experimental design following established watermarking evaluation practices
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: Theorem 3.1 provides no convergence guarantees for the fixed-point iteration, yet claims single iteration suffices; ε-parameterization fails empirically while δ-parameterization works better, suggesting the KL constraint is a poor quality proxy and undermining theoretical motivation

Performance highly sensitive to unmasking strategy: entropy-based remasking (which improves quality) substantially weakens watermark (Figure 6), creating deployment challenge since practitioners don't control DLM implementation choices

Limited security analysis: focuses only on detectability; watermark removal/spoofing discussed only briefly; no analysis of adaptive attacks; claimed improvements at higher |C| insufficiently rigorous
Quality degradation larger than claimed: 21% perplexity increase (1.56→1.90), GPT-4O score drop (8.95→8.43), and no human evaluation to assess for subtle artifacts
Top-k approximation in Algorithm 1 lacks error bounds; sensitivity to vocabulary size and hash space unexplored; could fail on specialized vocabularies

Incomplete practical deployment guidance: limited rationale for hyperparameter choices (why δ=4 vs δ=5?), unclear how to manage green list matrix in production, no discussion of different detection thresholds
Incomplete failure case analysis: no evaluation on very short sequences, structured domains (code/math), multi-lingual texts, or extreme parameter choices

strengths: First practical watermarking scheme for diffusion language models, addressing an important gap in an emerging paradigm
Principled constrained optimization framework with theoretical grounding (Theorem 3.1) and connection to existing ARLM watermarks
Comprehensive empirical evaluation: two DLM architectures, multiple remasking strategies, extensive ablations, robustness testing, and comparisons with multiple baselines
Strong empirical results: >99% TPR@1% FPR with minimal quality degradation, consistent across models and settings
Intuitive interpretation via expectation boost and predictive bias terms that provides genuine insight beyond formal optimality
Excellent reproducibility: detailed appendices, code provided, extensive hyperparameter specifications, computational resources disclosed
Practical algorithm (Algorithm 1) with manageable complexity O(nL|C||Σ|log|Σ|) and minimal generation overhead
weaknesses: Lack of convergence guarantees for the fixed-point iteration algorithm (Eq. 4) used in practice, despite only 1-3 iterations working empirically
ε-parameterization performing substantially worse than δ-parameterization (Fig. 4) suggests KL divergence may not appropriately control quality, but alternative proxies not explored
Limited experimental scope: only 2-3 DLM models tested, all modest in size (7-8B); generalization to larger models and diverse architectures unclear

Weak baseline comparison: the naive baseline (context-only watermarking) is the simplest possible adaptation; more sophisticated baselines (probabilistic context thresholding, entropy-based approaches) could be stronger

Incomplete security analysis: claims similarity to Red-Green watermarks which have known vulnerabilities; no discussion of attacks specific to diffusion setting or novel vulnerabilities from predictive bias term
Hash function design choices (SumHash, MinHash) not well justified; no exploration of alternative hash functions or comparison with distribution-optimized approaches
Detector unchanged from ARLM watermarks; no exploration of watermark-specific detectors that could exploit DLM-specific properties or the predictive bias structure
Top-k approximation (Algorithm 1) is significant practical simplification with unclear impact on theoretical guarantees and convergence

strengths: Addresses timely and well-motivated problem: First watermark for DLMs as these models rapidly emerge
Principled theoretical framework: Constrained optimization formulation with existence/uniqueness guarantees; recovers Red-Green ARLM watermarks in special case
Practical and efficient algorithm: Clear, implementable (O(nL|C||Σ| log |Σ|)), works with existing detectors without modification
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple models, extensive ablations across hash schemes/components/parameterizations, multiple attack types, both generation and infilling tasks
Strong empirical results: 99% TPR@1% FPR substantially outperforms baselines (~63-83%), robust to 30% local edits, minimal detection overhead
Intuitive decomposition: Expectation boost and predictive bias terms provide valuable insights into how watermarking works in diffusion setting
Reproducibility: Code will be released, extensive experimental details in appendices
weaknesses: Fixed-point iteration lacks theoretical guarantees: While Section 4.3 shows empirically single iterations work well, no convergence analysis provided—significant gap given emphasis on principled optimization
Quality-utility tradeoff inadequately addressed: Log perplexity increases 22% (1.56→1.90) at TPR@1; no human evaluation; GPT-4O scoring is limited
Limited experimental scope: Only 8B/7B models tested (scalability unclear); 600 prompts is modest; random remasking somewhat artificial; no sophisticated adversarial attacks
ε-parameterization failure poorly explained: Dramatic performance gap vs. δ-parameterization suggests optimization framework may not perfectly capture practical watermarking objective
Incomplete security analysis: No novel security analysis for DLM setting; reliance on cited work from ARLM context; potential vulnerabilities not discussed
Weak baseline comparison: Naive adaptation is somewhat strawman; more sophisticated probabilistic baselines could have been explored; limited comparison settings with AAR/KTH
Hash function design not novel: SumHash/MinHash borrowed from prior work; minimal impact of hash choice (Fig. 4) questions whether novel designs needed
Presentation density: 38-page paper with extensive appendices; connection between Eq. 3 and Algorithm 1 could be clearer; global definition of G ∈ {0,1}^{H×Σ} introduced late

strengths: First watermarking scheme specifically designed for diffusion language models, addressing a genuine and timely gap as DLMs gain traction
Solid theoretical framework with constrained optimization formulation (Eqs. 1-3) and rigorous Lagrangian analysis; elegantly recovers Red-Green ARLM watermarks as special case
Strong empirical results achieving >99% TPR@1%FPR across multiple models (LLADA-8B, DREAM-7B) with minimal computational overhead (~9ms/token)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablations (hashing schemes, components, parameterization, remasking strategies), robustness testing, and evaluation on multiple tasks
Insightful interpretation via expectation boost and predictive bias components, providing intuitive understanding of watermark mechanism
Excellent reproducibility with promised code release, detailed experimental setup, computational resources documented, and sufficient ablations for reproducibility
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and logical organization; addresses practical problem with emerging model class
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: fixed-point iteration lacks convergence guarantees to q*; authors acknowledge this but pragmatically use single iteration based on empirical performance rather than theory

KL-divergence constraint shown to be imperfect quality proxy (ε-parameterization yields much worse results); paper acknowledges this but relies on pragmatic δ-parameterization without theoretical justification

Notable quality degradation on benchmark accuracy (Table 3), particularly DREAM-7B with concerning drops on MBPP and GSM8K; authors acknowledge 'non-negligible drop in accuracy' but limited analysis provided
Limited security analysis for DLM-specific setting; paper claims same security as Red-Green but doesn't analyze potential attacks exploiting non-autoregressive generation and order-flexibility
Hash distribution computation only efficient for restricted families (SumHash, MinHash); 'no self-hashing assumption' is artificial (Fig. 20 shows SelfHash performs comparably)
Evaluation limited to relatively small models (≤8B parameters) and task diversity; robustness to paraphrasing/back-translation still significantly reduced as in ARLMs
Comparison primarily with weak order-agnostic baselines (Unigram, PatternMark); limited comparison with more sophisticated watermarking approaches

strengths: Novel problem: First watermark for DLMs, an important emerging paradigm
Principled theoretical framework: Constrained optimization formulation with clean solution (Theorem 3.1) and recovery of Red-Green as special case
Comprehensive evaluation: Multiple models, extensive ablations, robustness testing, and thoughtful baseline comparisons (Unigram, PatternMark)
Strong empirical results: >99% TPR@1% FPR with reasonable computational overhead
Intuitive interpretation: Decomposition into expectation boost and predictive bias terms clarifies the method
Thorough reproducibility: Detailed appendices, experimental protocols, computational resources documented
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: Primarily adapts existing Red-Green watermarks via marginalization; optimization framework is standard; represents engineering rather than conceptual advance
Overstated quality claims: Benchmark accuracy shows non-trivial drops (e.g., DREAM-7B GSM8K 38%→24% for some hyperparameters); 'minimal quality degradation' unsupported
Weak baseline comparison: Naive approach (context-available only) rather than principled alternative adaptation; more sophisticated Red-Green baseline needed
Theory-practice gaps: Theorem 3.1 lacks convergence guarantees; single-iteration practice contradicts theory; no explanation for why convergence guarantees unnecessary

Design choices unexplored: Top-k approximation justification missing; ε-parameterization's catastrophic failure (Fig. 4) suggests potential optimization problem misspecification; no self-hashing exploration
Limited model diversity: Only two models tested (LLADA-8B, DREAM-7B); single temperature (T=0.5); evaluation at different T than benchmarks
Security gaps: Inherits Red-Green vulnerabilities (spoofing/scrubbing); no DLM-specific defenses proposed; robustness to paraphrasing notably decreases

Presentation issues: Dense notation with critical details in appendices; unclear connection between full-sequence optimization (Eq. 1) and per-step Algorithm 2; confusing ε/δ parameterization discussion

strengths: Novel contribution: First principled watermarking approach for DLMs, addressing important emerging problem
Elegant theoretical framework: Clean constrained optimization formulation (Eq. 1) with existence/uniqueness theorem, naturally extends ARLM watermarks
Strong experimental results: >99% TPR@1%FPR across models with comprehensive ablations and robustness testing
Thorough evaluation: Multiple models, remasking strategies, diffusion steps, quality metrics, and Type-I error analysis
Good presentation: Clear exposition with intuitive Figure 1, well-structured theory, comprehensive appendices
Reproducibility: Code available, detailed experimental setup, documented hardware resources
Practical implementation: Minimal overhead (+9ms/token), simple Algorithm 2, multiple hash options, fast convergence
weaknesses: Lack of convergence guarantees: Fixed-point iteration used in practice lacks theoretical guarantees; authors acknowledge 'despite lack of theoretical guarantees' improvements occur empirically

KL constraint issues: ε-parameterization dramatically underperforms δ-parameterization (Fig. 4), suggesting constraint may be poorly chosen; authors acknowledge it's 'imperfect' but propose no alternative
Non-trivial quality impact: DREAM-7B benchmarks show significant drops (6% relative accuracy loss on some benchmarks); human evaluation missing
Limited scope: Only 2 primary DLM architectures (7-8B models); unclear generalization to larger/smaller models or diverse architectures
Inadequate security analysis: Relies on Red-Green detector; DLM-specific attacks not explored; arbitrary generation order may enable new vulnerabilities not addressed
Under-justified design choices: No self-hashing assumption lacks principled justification; Appendix H shows it works similarly, suggesting unnecessarily restrictive
Robustness limitations: Paraphrasing/back-translation significantly degrade detectability (Fig. 3 right); limited threat model definition
Hyperparameter guidance: Limited practical guidance on selecting δ, top-k for new models; recommendations appear somewhat arbitrary
